methodology.paper: Earlier Decision on Detection of Ransomware Identification: A Comprehensive Systematic Literature Review (Albshaier et al. 2024)
methodology.value: PRISMA-guided study selection (flow diagram in Section 2) filtering systematic-search results from academic databases plus industry reports and case studies, restricted to 2020-2024 publications. Contribution: categorisation of early-ransomware-detection approaches into signature-based, behaviour-pattern-based and machine-learning-based methods, assessment of their effectiveness, discussion of new trends, and identification of gaps, to guide proactive detection design. Verified against the MDPI article page, its abstract, and the Semantic Scholar record.

methodology.paper: A Survey on Ransomware: Evolution, Taxonomy, and Defense Solutions (Oz et al. 2022, ACM Computing Surveys)
methodology.value: Structured literature synthesis of 137 studies (1989-2020) across three target platforms (PCs/workstations, mobile devices, IoT/CPS). Contributions: detailed ransomware evolution narrative from early disk-encryptingPoC families to modern double-extortion campaigns; analysis of key ransomware building blocks (infection vectors, payload, hybrid encryption, C&C, anti-analysis); a taxonomy of notable ransomware families; platform-wise categorisation of defense research into analysis, detection (cryptographic, behaviour- and network-based, ML, rule-based/formal-methods/hybrid) and recovery (backups, key-derivation). Verified against ACM DL full record and the arXiv accepted-version PDF.

key_findings.paper: Earlier Decision on Detection of Ransomware Identification: A Comprehensive Systematic Literature Review (Albshaier et al. 2024)
key_findings.value: Early detection before encryption is feasible only by combining warning signs, frameworks and proactive techniques; signature-only approaches fail against ever-changing samples while behaviour- and ML-based approaches offer the strongest proactive direction as long as features (API calls, file I/O anomalies, network behaviours) are captured pre-execution; the review enumerates gaps in current research and stresses that detection technology must evolve continuously with the ransomware threat landscape.

key_findings.paper: A Survey on Ransomware: Evolution, Taxonomy, and Defense Solutions (Oz et al. 2022, ACM Computing Surveys)
key_findings.value: First survey to jointly cover evolution, taxonomy and defense across workstation, mobile and IoT/CPS platforms: documents the shift from simple locker/crypto families toward target-of-choice, double-extortion and platform-diversified operations; shows detection research is dominated by workstation-focused ML/behavioural methods while IoT/CPS defense studies rely almost exclusively on network-activity features; derives an extensive list of open research issues (evasion, portable-platform coverage, IoT/CPS defenses, lack of unified evaluation).

limitations.paper: Earlier Decision on Detection of Ransomware Identification: A Comprehensive Systematic Literature Review (Albshaier et al. 2024)
limitations.value: Restricted time window (2020-2024) and English-language emphasis limits coverage of the long pre-2020 detection canon and non-English literature; qualitative assessment of effectiveness - no standardised quantitative re-benchmarking of the surveyed detectors; MDPI special-issue review so inclusion criteria beyond the PRISMA flow are self-imposed; observed limitation: only a single lateral perspective (early detection), excluding payment/economics and incident-response literature.

limitations.paper: A Survey on Ransomware: Evolution, Taxonomy, and Defense Solutions (Oz et al. 2022, ACM Computing Surveys)
limitations.value: Coverage stops at studies published through 2020, pre-dating the 2021-2024 surge in double-extortion RaaS, leak sites and healthcare-focused campaigns; narrative (non-PRISMA) search process limits reproducibility of the corpus; no quantitative meta-comparison of reported detection accuracies across platforms.

research_gaps.paper: Earlier Decision on Detection of Ransomware Identification: A Comprehensive Systematic Literature Review (Albshaier et al. 2024)
research_gaps.value: Explicitly points out gaps in current early-detection research: insufficient benchmark datasets and standardised evaluation; weak pre-encryption behaviour coverage; limited integration of ML with frameworks and industry indicators; calls for strong, proactive, continuously updated detection systems as the future direction.

research_gaps.paper: A Survey on Ransomware: Evolution, Taxonomy, and Defense Solutions (Oz et al. 2022, ACM Computing Surveys)
research_gaps.value: Provides the extensive open-issues list used as the comparison baseline for the present review: no study existed giving a complete platform-diverse picture of ransomware and defenses; gaps include IoT/CPS defense research, recovery research, evaluation-uniformity, evading/anti-analysis countermeasures, and mobile-ransomware coverage.
